Anatomy of a ship

The floating city

A 362-metre cruise ship is a power station, a hotel and a 100,000-tonne boat at the same time. Follow the camera through the six systems that keep it afloat, moving and calm.

Numbers are for an Oasis-class ship: 361.8 m long, 47 m wide at the waterline, 9.3 m draft, about 100,000 t displacement, six Wärtsilä 46 diesel generators (97 MW), three 20 MW ABB Azipods, four 5.5 MW bow thrusters, four evaporators making 3,300 t of fresh water a day. Hotel load and full-load deadweight are typical figures, not published ones.
